edges.reason: onlyOwner modifier compares msg.sender to owner, gating transferOwnership.
acceptOwnership requires msg.sender == newOwner before changing ownership.
approve writes the allowance for msg.sender.
transfer burns and moves the msg.sender balance and checks the admin exemption.
receive() forwards the value back to the untrusted msg.sender.
block.timestamp feeds the launch-window comparison inside transfer.
block.timestamp is hashed into the pseudo-random burn percentage.
transfer branches on block.timestamp to set firstBlock and choose the transfer limits.
Unchecked multiplication result is used as the numerator of getPercentOfTrade.
The timestamp comparison decides whether launch-window limits apply in transfer.
Predictable block data determines the value returned by randNumber.
The external call in receive() is the sink of the fallback function.
transferOwnership writes the attacker-supplied value into newOwner, stage one of ownership takeover.
acceptOwnership reads newOwner to promote it and later clears it.
acceptOwnership overwrites owner with newOwner, completing the ownership transfer.
TradeUp constructor mints 1011 ether into _totalSupply.
TradeUp constructor credits the deployer balance.
TradeUp constructor sets the MinSupply floor to 10 ether.
TradeUp constructor records msg.sender as AdminAddress, the launch-window privileged account.
burn() calls _burn(msg.sender, _amount) reducing _totalSupply.
burn() accumulates the burned amount into totalBurnt.
transfer calls getPercentOfTrade to enforce the 3% post-launch cap.
transfer calls _burn for the random amount, reducing _totalSupply.
transfer calls _transfer for the unburnt remainder.
transfer calls randNumber, which relies on miner-controlled block data.
transfer sets the firstTransfer latch flag.
transfer writes firstBlock from block.timestamp, defining the launch window.
transfer adds the burned amount to totalBurnt.
transferFrom delegates to _transferFrom.
_burn reduces _totalSupply and must stay above MinSupply.
_transferFrom performs the underlying _transfer.
_transferFrom reduces the allowance through _approve.
approve delegates the allowance write to _approve.
increaseAllowance writes the new allowance via _approve.
decreaseAllowance writes the new allowance via _approve.
_transfer reads and writes both sides of _balances.
_approve writes the nested _allowances mapping.
Untrusted _newOwner becomes the pending owner, enabling ownership takeover after acceptOwnership.
Caller supplied _amount flows into burn().
numTokens is multiplied by 1000 without an overflow-safe helper.
numTokens is the input of the percentage computation.
The public transfer amount is checked against the launch-window and 3% caps.
The recipient balance is checked against the 2 ether launch-window cap.
The transfer amount reaches the unchecked multiplication inside getPercentOfTrade.
The transfer amount determines the random burn amount through multiplication and division.
The computed burn amount is passed to _burn.
The computed burn amount is added to totalBurnt.
The random percentage scales the transfer amount into the burn amount.
The random value derives from the miner-influenced hash in randNumber.
msg.value captured in receive is forwarded to the caller in the external call.
numerator holds the unchecked product that can overflow.
temp performs the division by _totalSupply inside the percentage computation.
percent is the value returned by getPercentOfTrade.
The initial owner argument is stored by the ownership-module constructor.
The constructor assigns the owner state variable.
The _name constructor argument is accepted but immediately overwritten.
The _symbol constructor argument is accepted but immediately overwritten.
The constructor hard-codes the name to a URL string.
The constructor hard-codes the symbol to TRADEUP.
The constructor fixes decimals to 18.
transfer reads _balances[msg.sender] and _balances[recipient] and writes both.
The _sender argument flows into transferFrom.
The _recipient argument flows into transferFrom.
The _amount argument flows into transferFrom.
